title: Walter Page's Blue Devils, Rushing and Basie moving to Moten
summary: He describes Walter Page's Blue Devils, how Jimmy Rushing left first, then Basie, joining Bennie Moten.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, I'll tell you what had happened. Walter Page had the greatest band that I ever heard in my life. Now remember, I was running around, Milt. I used to go to Detroit and what have you when they had Edwards
JONES 33

Collegians and when they had these band contests, when they had McKinney Cotton Pickers, when they had before Blanche Calloway, and Johnson Happy Pals, and Zack Whyte, and all that. But Bennie Moten -
Walter Page?
Walter Page had the band, the Blue Devils. The first one to leave him was Hot Lips Page - no, the first one to leave was Jimmie Rushing, then Basie, then Hot Lips Page.
Basie was working in Bennie Moten's band?
He was working with Walter Page.
Oh, I mean you said the first one that left Bennie Moten's band -
No, no, no, no, the first one to leave Walter Page's band was Jimmie Rushing, the vocalist, because he and Fathead with McKinney Cotton Pickers, they sounded alike if you'd turn your back.
Who was Walter Page's piano player?
Charlie Washington. Short-lived and, Lord have mercy, it's too bad that they didn't record then!
So then Jimmie Rushing left Walter Page?
He left Walter Page.

Jo, I want to stop a minute here to go to the phone... I'm going to go back to this and, let's see, we're back with Walter Page's band. Walter Page had this great band with Charlie Washington playing piano and Walter Page with his Blue Devils. Now Jimmie Rushing you say was
JONES 34
the first one to leave the band, right? Jimmie, to go to Bennie Moten, and then he brought Basie in.
Who brought Basie - Walter Page?
Yes.
Into the Blue Devils?
Into Bennie Moten. Jimmie Rushing left first and then Basie left and joined Bennie.
Bennie didn't play piano then; Basie played piano for him, huh?
(End of tape reel II)
